2609.00090.title: Assessing Alignment and Stability of Feature Importance Explanations via Weight of Evidence
2609.00090.paper_summary: Feature importance Methods (FIMs) are widely used in Explainable AI to interpret model predictions, yet attribution scores alone often provide limited insight into the underlying reasoning process. In this work, we introduce a novel perspective by embedding FIMs within a hypothesis-testing framework based on Weight of Evidence (WoE). We quantify how strongly the observed evidence supports any given hypothesis on feature importance. The reference hypothesis can stem from domain knowledge, ground truth, or be derived from the FIM itself. This formulation enables a principled evaluation of FIMs, capturing both their alignment with prior knowledge and their variability. We further provide theoretical results linking WoE to attribution variance. Empirical results shows the applicability and flexibility of our strategy analyzing LIME and SHAP explanations in settings with different reference hypotheses. Overall, our framework offers a complementary tool for assessing FIMs through a contrastive, evidence-based lens.
2609.00090.paper_summary_zh: 特徵重要性方法（FIMs）在可解釋的人工智慧中被廣泛用於解釋模型預測，但單靠歸因分數通常對於潛在的推理過程提供的見解有限。<lb/>在這項工作中，我們通過將FIMs嵌入基於證據權重（WoE）的假設檢驗框架中，引入了一種新穎的視角。<lb/>我們量化觀察到的證據在多大程度上支持任何給定的特徵重要性假設。<lb/>參考假設可以源自領域知識、真實情況，或從FIM本身推導而來。<lb/>這種表述使得對FIMs進行原則性評估成為可能，捕捉它們與先前知識的對齊程度及其變異性。<lb/>我們進一步提供理論結果，將WoE與歸因變異聯繫起來。<lb/>實證結果顯示我們的策略在分析LIME和SHAP解釋時，在不同參考假設的情境下的適用性和靈活性。<lb/>總體而言，我們的框架提供了一種通過對比的、基於證據的視角來評估FIMs的補充工具。
